summary: André Caquot was a religious studies scholar and linguist who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, École Normale Supérieure, and École Pratique des Hautes Études. He held posts at the EPHE (~1955–1972), University of Strasbourg, University of Paris, and Collège de France (1972–1994).

André Couture is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Laval University, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and Paris-Sorbonne University. He held an academic post at Laval University from around 1980 to 2010.

André Godard was an archaeology, history, and Iranian studies specialist who studied at the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts. He served at the DAFA in 1923 and as Director General of Iran's Archaeological Service (~1928–1960) and University of Tehran (~1934–1940).

Linguist André Martinet studied at ENS, Humboldt University, and the Sorbonne under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes. He held posts at EPHE (1938–1946), Columbia University (1947–1955), University of Paris (~1955–1970), and Paris Descartes University (~1955–1977).
Linguist André Mazon studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1900–1904) and Charles University (~1904–1905). He held a post at the Collège de France from 1923 to 1951.
André Oltramare served as Professor of Latin at the University of Geneva from around 1856 to 1888, where he succeeded Paul Oltramare.

Indologist André Padoux studied at Institut de Civilisation Indienne and under teachers including Louis Renou and Swami Lakshman Joo. He served as director of Institut Français Frankfurt (~1959–1964) and Directeur de Recherche at the CNRS (~1964–1985).
André Wedemeyer worked in Sinology, Japanology, and linguistics. He completed his doctoral studies under August Conrady and held an academic post at the University of Leipzig.

Buddhist studies and Indology scholar Andy Rotman studied at CIHTS and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins. He held posts at Smith College (attested 2013–2026) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2026).

Anett Krause, working in Indology and computation, studied at Leipzig, Halle-Wittenberg, and Marburg. She held research posts at Marburg, Halle-Wittenberg, the Mainz Academy, and the Royal Library of Berlin (2023).

Angela Falco Howard is an archaeologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist. She completed her doctoral dissertation at New York University under Alexander Coburn Soper and later held a professorship at Rutgers University (attested 2005).
Specializing in Tibetology, Angela Manderscheid held academic posts at the Free University of Berlin and as a researcher at the University of Oulu (attested 1998).

Angela Sumegi, who works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, completed her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa studying under Nalini Devdas. She was an assistant professor at Carleton University's College of the Humanities (attested 2008).
Angela Zito, a scholar of religious studies and sinology, earned her Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1978–1989). She became an associate professor at New York University in 1999.

Philosopher Angelika Krebs studied at Freiburg, New College, Berkeley, Konstanz, and Frankfurt, earning her doctorate under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Konstanz, Frankfurt (1993–2001), and the University of Basel (chair in practical philosophy, 2001).

Indologist Angelika Malinar studied at Mainz and Tübingen, completing her PhD and habilitation there. She held teaching posts at SOAS (~2000–2007) and the University of Zurich, where she became an associate professor of Indology in 2009.
Angelo Brelich was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Erzsébet University (~1933–1937) and held a post at Sapienza University of Rome from around 1942 to 1977.

Indologist and linguist Angelo De Gubernatis studied at the University of Turin and Humboldt University under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at the Istituto di Studi Superiori di Firenze (1863–1890) and Sapienza University of Rome (1890–1908).

Angelo Francesco Saverio Maffei was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Seminario Maggiore Arcivescovile di Trento and the Pontifical Gregorian University. He served as Rector of St Aloysius College (1891–1896) and was a Fellow of the University of Madras.

Indologist Angelo Maria Pizzagalli studied at the University of Pisa under Carlo Formichi. He held teaching posts in Sanskrit and Indian civilization at the University of Pisa (1913), University of Genoa (1914), and University of Milan (~1924–1944).
